title: NATO Releases Official Quantum Technology Roadmap Establishing Operational Timelines and Standardization Frameworks - Quantum Computing Report
author: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
text:
Following the formal approval by NATO Allies on July 30, 2026, the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) has published the public summary of its Quantum Technology Roadmap. Functioning as the operational implementation framework for the 2023 NATO Quantum Technology Strategy, the document establishes structured Lines of Effort (LoE) across quantum computing, quantum sensing, and quantum communications to accelerate technology adoption, maintain defense interoperability, and mitigate cryptographic security risks across the 32-nation alliance.

The roadmap outlines specific operational milestones overseen by the Digital Policy Committee (DPC) and executed across the NATO Enterprise—including Allied Command Transformation (ACT), Allied Command Operations (ACO), the NATO Communications and Information Agency (NCIA), the Science and Technology Organization (STO), the Defence Innovation Accelerator for the North Atlantic (DIANA), and the NATO Innovation Fund (NIF). Implementation is further supported by the Transatlantic Quantum Community (TQC) and its Industry Network, which recently expanded to include Belgium and Bulgaria alongside 22 Allies and six partner nations.

Strategic priorities emphasize quantum sensing applications for Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT) in GNSS-denied environments—validated through the STO Centre for Maritime Research and Experimentation (CMRE) QUESTOR trials in La Spezia, Italy. For secure communications, the Quantum Zero Beacon Project (QZBP) will establish a pilot link between NATO HQ in Brussels and SHAPE in Mons by Q4 2027 to validate operational quantum-resilient networking frameworks.
